title: Run comparing two register words
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, and let $r_1,r_2$ be distinct registers. Suppose the transitions at states $e_C,e_{By},e_{Bn}$ implement, respectively, the bitwise comparison of the two registers, the comparison continuation leading to yes state $yes$, and the comparison continuation leading to no state $no$; assume none of these three states is a call state. If the two registers initially store words $w_1,w_2$, then for any words $u_1,u_2,pre$ with $w_1=pre\,u_1$ and $w_2=pre\,u_2$, there are a time $T$ and an integer position $p$ such that $|pre|-1\le p<|w_1|$, and the run from the comparison state with both heads at position $|pre|$ reaches state $e_{By}$ if $w_1=w_2$ and state $e_{Bn}$ otherwise, with both heads at position $p$. Before time $T$, the run remains in state $e_C$, with both heads at a common position $q$ satisfying $|pre|\le q\le |w_1|$.
hypotheses_covered: The transition at $e_C$ has the specified comparison behavior
The transitions at $e_{By}$ and $e_{Bn}$ have the specified continuation behavior
